fixes.from: CA Foundation / Intermediate / Final registered students. Multiple slabs — Merit-cum-Need has income cap ₹3L.
fixes.to: Students registered with ICAI for the CA Foundation, Intermediate or Final course (Final students must have started articleship). The needs-based scholarships ask that parents' income be no more than ₹5 lakh a year, certified by a practising chartered accountant (Foundation and Intermediate) or the articleship principal (Final). The ₹5,000-a-month merit award, for Intermediate rank holders 1 to 10 who have registered for Final and started articleship, lists no income condition. ICAI's flyer says an announcement on a revised scheme will be published on its Self-Service Portal shortly.
fixes.why: The row's note names a ₹3 lakh income cap. ICAI's flyer sets parents' income at no more than Rs 5,00,000 a year for every needs-based scholarship (Foundation, Intermediate, Final, and Final for Intermediate ranks 11-50) and lists no income condition for the merit award (Intermediate ranks 1-10). The page prints this note beside the new rolling line and in its eligibility FAQ answer (FAQPage JSON-LD). The row has no incomeMaxLakhs, so the matcher has no income gate for ICAI, and none is added: a ₹5 lakh gate would turn away the merit-award rank holders, for whom the flyer sets no income condition. The flyer's line on a revised scheme is kept, so a student knows the figures may change.

fixes.why: The row's '₹1,500-₹2,500/month' leaves out the Final-course amounts on ICAI's own flyer: Rs 4,000 a month for Intermediate ranks 11-50 and the Rs 5,000-a-month merit award for ranks 1-10. The flyer's periods are 4 months (Foundation), 8 months plus up to 3 + 3 (Intermediate), and 24 months or the rest of articleship, whichever is less (Final).
